versions.text: Standard: The air vehicle is designed with margin to withstand the induced vibration and acoustic environments for the DSL accounting for: a. All vibration and acoustic sources. b. Configurations. c. Flight and ground operations. d. Design usage spectra. e. Safety factors. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination. (1) Verify the ASIP Master Plan or RSIP Master Plan, as specified in MIL-STD-1530 or MIL- STD-3063, respectively, documents the analysis and test verification methods required to certify the design for vibration and sonic fatigue; structural certification tasks are updated for modifications or changes to the air vehicle following initial AW certification basis; and all artifacts are developed IAW applicable sections of MIL-STD-1530 or MIL-STD-3063. (2) Verify detailed structural design criteria for vibration and sonic fatigue, as specified in MIL- STD-1530 or MIL-STD-3063, documents the requirements to achieve structural integrity. (3) Verify test plans are scoped to measure all metrics for vibration and sonic fatigue to allow for tracking margins to achieve envelope expansion. Analysis. (1) Verify the environment criteria documentation defines vibration and acoustic environments throughout the air vehicle; predicted environments consider all sources, ground and flight operational conditions, air vehicle configurations, and usage spectra; spectra compression and test exposure durations are traceable to equivalent operational exposure durations; and analytical predictions are updated and correlated with developmental and ground tests. (2) Verify initial vibration and sonic fatigue analysis models are updated and correlated with developmental tests; and analyses predictions are compliant with structural design criteria. Test. (1) Lab test: Verify developmental test results are used to update the environment criteria documentation and substantiate the vibration and sonic fatigue predictions. (2) Ground test: Verify vibration and acoustic ground tests substantiate the models used to update the environmental predictions. Prior to entering operational test or operations, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination. (4) Verify strength summary and operating restrictions define the operational envelope and necessary restrictions; reflect all analyses and tests; and satisfy the structural design criteria. (5) Verify the flight manual is consistent with the envelope and limitations defined in the strength summary and operating restrictions for all air vehicle configurations; and contains all necessary warnings, cautions, notes, emergency procedures, and inspection criteria required to operate in the design vibration and acoustic environments for the DSL. Analysis. (3) Verify the environment criteria documentation is updated with ground and flight tests to define the vibration and acoustic environments. (4) Verify vibration and sonic fatigue analysis models are updated and correlated to ground and flight test; and final analyses predictions are compliant with the structural design criteria and are incorporated into the final strength summary and operating restrictions. Test. (3) Flight or Ground test: Verify ground and flight test results are used to update the environment criteria documentation and substantiate the analytical vibration and sonic fatigue lives.
